in adult Kuwaiti males (n = 200) and females (n = 180), increase in body fat, measured as BMI >30 or as W/H >1, was associated with a significant restrictive effect on pulmonary ventilatory functions, without obstructive ventilatory impairment (FEV1 >80% of FVC).

central adiposity (waist-to-hip ratio) was associated with a significant restrictive impairment of pulmonary ventilatory function independent of sex, height or age, and increasing severity of obesity at BMI >30 was significantly associated with an increasing restrictive impairment of pulmonary ventilation with no evidence of obstruction.
